pull_request.title: Bundle Collision with SGM file
pull_request.body:
# Description:
We have an optimised & preprocessed file format called SGM that was written by Luomu but, for some reason, we don't ship SGM files in with the main distribution. Part of that reason was that it helped loading times a lot but not as much as it could have due to the collision mesh generation being excluded from it.

With the merging of #3099 giving us 3 very complex new space stations and very complex collision meshes I've tried to add support for serialising and deserialising the collision meshes into our SGM format.

## Distribution:
With this change it would make sense to build the `.SGM` files in-place, delete the `.DAE` from the build and only have them in Git and `pioneer-assets`. 
This way players don't have to worry about having the correct files or building `.SGM` versions.

# Loading times:
A quick comparison, please note that this is done on my laptop with a 512GiB SSD so there's little variation due to disk access, but possibly some due to thermal throttling/behaviour.

## SGM Load times:
I did 3 runs and the times were
* Loading took: 23865.460385 milliseconds
* Loading took: 23486.056590 milliseconds
* Loading took: 23832.089322 milliseconds
For an average of **~23727.87** milliseconds.

## Standard Load times:
Once again but with no SGM files.
* Loading took: 128687.466982 milliseconds
* Loading took: 126967.270705 milliseconds
* Loading took: 126556.816863 milliseconds
For an average of **~127403.85** milliseconds

## Result:
This means that using SGM files with the collision mesh data results in the game loading to the intro screen **~5.37** times faster.

# At the Command line:
**WARNING**: The SGM files this creates will be chosen in preference to the original data in future so you might miss updates to files. Best to delete all of these SGM files after experimenting with this **WARNING**

To recreate the SGM files you just need to build the ModelCompiler, this should be shipped with the binaries versions, or you can build it yourself. It's built alongside Pioneer.
Simply go to the Pioneer folder where ModelCompiler & Pioneer reside, open a prompt / terminal and enter something like: `modelcompiler -b inplace`
That will create an SGM file for every model in the game and place it next to it's `.model` file.

# Status:
Worth testing, as I've just fixed the bug I had caused and collision now works again. Loads fast and works!

I've chosen to **compress** all of the SGM files the modelcompilier produces as this results in a reduction from ~132MB down to just ~39.5MB which is a significant reduction. It does have a negative impact on the loading times, raising it from an average 20 seconds to 24 seconds. However I think this is more than worth it.

Andy

issue.title: Bundle Collision with SGM file
issue.body:
# Description:
We have an optimised & preprocessed file format called SGM that was written by Luomu but, for some reason, we don't ship SGM files in with the main distribution. Part of that reason was that it helped loading times a lot but not as much as it could have due to the collision mesh generation being excluded from it.

With the merging of #3099 giving us 3 very complex new space stations and very complex collision meshes I've tried to add support for serialising and deserialising the collision meshes into our SGM format.

## Distribution:
With this change it would make sense to build the `.SGM` files in-place, delete the `.DAE` from the build and only have them in Git and `pioneer-assets`. 
This way players don't have to worry about having the correct files or building `.SGM` versions.

# Loading times:
A quick comparison, please note that this is done on my laptop with a 512GiB SSD so there's little variation due to disk access, but possibly some due to thermal throttling/behaviour.

## SGM Load times:
I did 3 runs and the times were
* Loading took: 23865.460385 milliseconds
* Loading took: 23486.056590 milliseconds
* Loading took: 23832.089322 milliseconds
For an average of **~23727.87** milliseconds.

## Standard Load times:
Once again but with no SGM files.
* Loading took: 128687.466982 milliseconds
* Loading took: 126967.270705 milliseconds
* Loading took: 126556.816863 milliseconds
For an average of **~127403.85** milliseconds

## Result:
This means that using SGM files with the collision mesh data results in the game loading to the intro screen **~5.37** times faster.

# At the Command line:
**WARNING**: The SGM files this creates will be chosen in preference to the original data in future so you might miss updates to files. Best to delete all of these SGM files after experimenting with this **WARNING**

To recreate the SGM files you just need to build the ModelCompiler, this should be shipped with the binaries versions, or you can build it yourself. It's built alongside Pioneer.
Simply go to the Pioneer folder where ModelCompiler & Pioneer reside, open a prompt / terminal and enter something like: `modelcompiler -b inplace`
That will create an SGM file for every model in the game and place it next to it's `.model` file.

# Status:
Worth testing, as I've just fixed the bug I had caused and collision now works again. Loads fast and works!

I've chosen to **compress** all of the SGM files the modelcompilier produces as this results in a reduction from ~132MB down to just ~39.5MB which is a significant reduction. It does have a negative impact on the loading times, raising it from an average 20 seconds to 24 seconds. However I think this is more than worth it.

Andy

comment.body: Tested with Linux/Windows with and without sgm files, it's no worse without and them and much better with them so have merged.

issue.title: generic linear-algebra functions for Number types (e.g. BigFloat)
issue.body:
It would be nice to have linear-algebra functions for `BigFloat` (possibly as an external package?) and other generic `Number` types.

Currently, `\` on a `BigFloat` converts to `Float64`; `eig` and `qr` don't work at all.

The good news is that LINPACK-style triple-loop textbook implementations (straight out of Trefethen or Golub & Van Loan) should mostly suffice.  Since `BigFloat` operations are CPU-limited rather than memory-limited, there is no reason to implement a LAPACK/BLAS-style blocked algorithm.

cc: @andrioni

cpufreq: Always allow update of user policy

maintained in policy min and max thus changing the limits for verification

current user policy min/max with the updated values if any. This would take
care of cases uwhere user policy min/max input is higher/lesser than the

cpufreq: Resolve CPUFREQ_NOTIFY issue

When the cpufreq_stat receives the frequency policy notification,
it checks if the frequency table and stats table are present for the cpu.
If both are present, it returns with -EBUSY error to the notification.
Due to this, none of the other registered modules receive this
notification.

If the stat table and sysfs nodes are already created, return 0 instead
of returning EBUSY error.

Signed-off-by: Pranav Vashi <neobuddy89@gmail.com>

cpufreq / stats: fix race between stats allocation and first usage

This patch forces complete struct cpufreq_stats allocation for all cpus before
registering CPUFREQ_TRANSITION_NOTIFIER notifier, otherwise in some conditions
cpufreq_stat_notifier_trans() can be called in the middle of stats allocation,
in this case cpufreq_stats_table already exists, but stat->freq_table is NULL.

issue.title: dist/material-styleguide.html doesn't load correctly [material-sprint]
issue.body:
In the material-sprint branch, the statically-built version of `material-styleguide.html` (i.e. the version in `dist/material-styleguide.html` created by `gulp`) usually doesn't load correctly from localhost--the main content frame appears to be blank.

To reproduce:

````sh
$ git checkout material-sprint
$ gulp
$ cd dist
$ python -m SimpleHTTPServer
$ open http://localhost:8000/material-styleguide.html # no content in main frame >50% of the time
````

This seems to happen if the browser is able to load the styleguide-demo iframes before sizeDemo() is [able to attach the onload handlers](https://github.com/google/web-starter-kit/blob/material-sprint/app/material-styleguide.html#L174), and so some are never called, which means the `demosLoaded` class is never added to `<body>`. (Which is more likely to happen if loading from localhost, without browser-sync being involved.)

issue.title: dist/material-styleguide.html doesn't load correctly [material-sprint]
issue.body:

To reproduce:

````sh

This seems to happen if the browser is able to load the styleguide-demo iframes before sizeDemo() is [able to attach the onload handlers](https://github.com/google/web-starter-kit/blob/material-sprint/app/material-styleguide.html#L174), and so some are never called, which means the `demosLoaded` class is never added to `<body>`. (Which is more likely to happen if loading from localhost, without browser-sync being involved.)

comment.body:
I've been able to reproduce this locally. We're currently rewriting the material-styleguide.html implementation to move away from iframes as much as possible. This work hasn't yet been checked in to the material-sprint branch, but soon you will just have a static HTML file with all of the markup existing in the same file so this issue will disappear.

cc @gauntface as an FYI that this is currently occurring.

issue.title: Tabular columns in mathmode (for .html and others)
issue.body:
When we write code like the following in `.xml` ``` d (days worked)p (cents)1 2 2 4 3 8 4 16 5 32 10 1024 30 1073741824
``` we translate into `.tex` and receive ``` \begin{tabular}{S[table-format=2.0]S[table-format=10.0]} \beforeheading \heading{$d$ (days worked)}&\heading{$p$ (cents)}\\ \afterheading 1 &2 \\\normalline 2 &4 \\\normalline 3 &8 \\\normalline 4 &16 \\\normalline 5 &32 \\\normalline 10 &1024 \\\normalline 30 &1073741824\\\lastline \end{tabular} ``` The `.tex` version uses the `siunitx` package which automatically puts each entry into mathmode. The `.html` version isn't quite as clever--any ideas on how we can fix this? One possible (clumsy, heavy) solution is to put each entry into a new tag, perhaps `` for 'conditional mathmode' which would do nothing in the `.tex` version, and put the entry into `mathmode` for `.html` and other versions. In such a scheme the above snippet might look like, for example, ```1 2 2 4 ``` This raises a more general question: when we hit questions/issues such as this, should we stop until they're resolved, or just plough forward?

comment.body:
I like the syntax you're suggesting, it makes a lot of sense. The only part of it that worries me is the implementation (!)....

If we go down this route of re-building an `siunit`-style syntax, should we re-build all of the other `LaTeX` syntax as well, e.g `\frac{1}{2}`? Or is that a separate issue?

pull_request.title: [WIP] major refactoring of architecture
pull_request.body:
|Q            |A  |
|---          |---|
|Bug Fix?     |yes|
|New Feature? |yes |
|BC Breaks?   |*yes!** |
|Deprecations?|no |
|Fixed Tickets| #26  |
|License      |MIT|

This a major refactoring of the search system architecture.

In summary the following has changed;

## ConditionOptimizers 

Formatters are renamed to ConditionOptimizers, and have an optional priority for sorting.

## Input processor changes

View to normalized value transformation now happens in the Input processor.
The SearchConditionBuilder does not use this technique.

Range bounds are now validated when processing, and not as an *optional* process afterwards.

To make InputProcessors reusable, configuration must be provided as first parameter of `process()`.

And last, all processors when testing now share the same assertions to ensure a correct result.

## Values 

To make locking the SearchCondition state easier and enforce a stricter OOP architecture value objects are now immutable and marked final.

`PatternMatch::getViewValue()` is removed as this method doesn't make sense for a string-only value object.

## Symfony validator

The Symfony validator extension is **finally** moved to its own repository and package.
As constraint validation is no longer needed for validating range-bounds.

## TODO

- [ ] Add support for locking the ValuesGroup and FieldSet.
- [ ] Check documentation for inconsistent usage of terms.
- [ ] Make tests for exporters uniform (same like input).
- [ ] Look for missing tests and documentation.

issue.title: Loop fix
issue.body:
Converted most of the `while True` loops to explicit `for` loops looping over a length after which the pattern repeats, then raise an error if the pattern hasn't broken by then. This should produce a desirable behavior that fixes #4 (though I think that there are certain endless-loop conditions which I'm currently only detecting in the iterator, not the constructor, because checking them in the constructor would involve a much more complicated logic because they involve interactions between the `byhour`, `byminute` and/or `bysecond` rules - either way I think they're likely exceedingly rare in practice).

I did a little refactoring in the looping logic, but not much since I think a lot of it won't end up being used in `rrule2` anyway. I'm a bit curious as to why we're explicitly handling the low-level operations of incrementing the day rather than incrementing a `datetime.datetime` object using `datetime.timedelta` objects - is this for the sake of performance or something? I can't imagine it would add much overhead, and it would be much easier to maintain.

I also converted the `by_` tuples to sets, because it doesn't seem that their order is ever used, but there are frequent calls to `in`, which will be considerably sped up by the use of sets. While I was doing that, I did some refactoring in the constructor which will make it easier to switch back if this change proves undesirable.

c := cron.New()

c.Start()

3) Added a function NextNTimes for Entry struct which returns next (upto) N activation times.

issue.body:
In theory this should be faster, since secp256k1_fe_equal_var is able to
 shortcut the normalization.  On x86_64 the improvement appears to be in
 the noise for me.  At least it makes the code cleaner.

comment.body:
So, the current implied contract is that field elements have at most magnitude 8, which is verified in all field element operations.

The fe_sqrt routine however accepts a field element a (which, according to the contract can have magnitude up to 8), and is added to t1 (which has magnitude 2), so the addition could result in a field element with magnitude 10, which is not allowed. In practice, all existing code paths are _guaranteed_ (because the veirifcation of magnitudes is static and conservative) to never result in a having magnitude 8.

So the 'bug' could be fixed by just declaring that fe_sqrt takes an argument with magnitude at most 6 (which is already the case in practice).

+## Upgrade FROM 1.0.0-beta4 to 1.0.0-beta5
+
+There has been been some major refactoring to make the system more robust
+easier to use. 
+
+* The `Rollerworks\Component\Search\Formatter\TransformFormatter` is removed,
+  transforming is now performed in the Input processor.
+
+### Input
+
+* Input processors are now reusable, configuration (limiting) must be passed as the
+  first parameter of `Rollerworks\Component\Search\Input\InputProcessorInterface::process()`.
+  
+* Any error will throw an exception now (see User error handling below for information).
+  
+* Validation of ranges (correct bounds) is now performed when processing the Input (not after).
+  
+### User error handling
+
+Because its possible that a search-condition contains errors, each processor
+that has a transforming or validating role will throw an `Rollerworks\Component\Search\Exception\InvalidSearchValuesException`.
+
+The `InvalidSearchValuesException` still provides access to the search-condition,
+but the condition must be considered as none-final as some values can be invalid.
+  
+**Note:** The `InvalidSearchValuesException` is thrown *after* processing,
+so it contains all invalid values (and not just the first violation) in a field values list.
+
+A `ValuesGroup` object no longer keeps track of errors, getting the errors
+is now be asking each field for there errors-state. 
+
+**Note:** By default only the fields at current level are checked, pass `true` to `ValuesGroup::hasErrors()`
+to traverse the deeper error-state of all nested groups.
+
+### Validation
+
+The default validator (Validator extension) is moved to `rollerworks/search-symfony-validator`, 
+And no longer implements the old Formatter interface.

pull_request.title: [WIP] major refactoring of architecture
pull_request.body:
|Q            |A  |
|---          |---|
|Bug Fix?     |yes|
|New Feature? |yes |
|BC Breaks?   |*yes!** |
|Deprecations?|no |
|Fixed Tickets| #26  |
|License      |MIT|

This a major refactoring of the search system architecture.

In summary the following has changed;

## ConditionOptimizers 

Formatters are renamed to ConditionOptimizers, and have an optional priority for sorting.

## Input processor changes

View to normalized value transformation now happens in the Input processor.
The SearchConditionBuilder does not use this technique.

Range bounds are now validated when processing, and not as an *optional* process afterwards.

To make InputProcessors reusable, configuration must be provided as first parameter of `process()`.

And last, all processors when testing now share the same assertions to ensure a correct result.

## Values 

To make locking the SearchCondition state easier and enforce a stricter OOP architecture value objects are now immutable and marked final.

`PatternMatch::getViewValue()` is removed as this method doesn't make sense for a string-only value object.

## Symfony validator

The Symfony validator extension is **finally** moved to its own repository and package.
As constraint validation is no longer needed for validating range-bounds.

## TODO

- [ ] Add support for locking the ValuesGroup and FieldSet.
- [ ] Check documentation for inconsistent usage of terms.
- [ ] Make tests for exporters uniform (same like input).
- [ ] Look for missing tests and documentation.

issue.title: Using the history module breaks slug_candidates
issue.body:
I have a perfectly working model with:
```ruby
class Case < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.primary_key = :case_id
  friendly_id :slug_candidates, use: :slugged

  private

  def slug_candidates
    [
      :name,
      [:name, :full_citation]
    ]
  end
end
```

That has been working perfectly. I'm including the `primary_key` call just in case it's important.

Today I tried to add the `history` module like this:
```ruby
  friendly_id :slug_candidates, use: [:slugged, :history]
```

After that (and running the migration, etc) when I try to add a Case which has the same `name` as another existing one, I get a Postgres error saying the slug is not unique. It's not trying the second option in the `slug_candidates` array. Removing the `history` module makes it work again.

issue.title: 検索無しでも見やすい挟み込みリストを作る
issue.body:
## 理由
検索途中まで作ってみたけど、正直いらない。
理由は二つ。
* 普段から譜面みてるから、50~60行から必要情報探すのは苦ではない。
  むしろ検索条件考えるほうがめんどい

* ユーザーが挟み込み先を探す流れを検討し直したため。
  挟み込み先を最終的に確定させるのは楽団員（挟み込みに行く人）であり、
  その人が決断する理由はユーザーと異なる可能性がある。
  そのため、挟み込みリストの段階で絞り込んでしまうと、
  本来挟み込める楽団員が居た演奏会を省いてしまう危険性がある。
  このことから検索機能はユーザーの主目的である「演奏会の集客」に
  不利益を与える危険性があることから、破棄することとした。

## 実現したいこと

* 日付の区切りはハッキリと
* 各列（特に曲目、場所）は上から流し見で把握できること
 * DONE:文章を改行表示できる
 * 横スクロール操作は行わせない
   * 動作が増えて手間
    * ユーザーが楽団情報を読むのは「この楽団に挟み込みに行くor行かないの判断をする」
　ことが目的であり、それを最速で達成するためには、全情報が画面内にあることが必要なため。
* DONE:最寄り駅、場所情報いれなきゃなぁ
 * DONE:会場情報に会場名入れる
 * DONE:最寄り駅に最寄り駅情報入れる
   * DONE:そのためのDB作る
* 日付は外だししよう
* DONEスクレイピングエラーと向き合う
 * 保留：エンコーディングエラー
 * DONE元サイト楽団HPのリンク切れ
   * DONE:2014/1１件目、楽団HPが現在ページを指している

## メモ
* これらが出来たら吹奏楽、合唱、演劇にも波及
  ※仮説※
  市民文化ホールでやるようなイベントは総じて挟み込みしているのかな？
  →調査しよう
* 東京外の演奏会はどうするかな？
  →東京外のひとも使うから排除するのは忍びないけど、
      リンクで外だしするのは全体のスピード感を損なう。
      どうしたものかなぁ。注釈でもいれとこうかなぁ。

issue.title: endless loop in rrule.py
issue.body:
There is a bug in rrule.py (dateutil 2.3). The `while True` loop on line 659 does not always terminate:
```python
elif freq == HOURLY:
    if filtered:
        # Jump to one iteration before next day
        hour += ((23-hour)//interval)*interval
    while True:
        hour += interval
        div, mod = divmod(hour, 24)
        if div:
            hour = mod
            day += div
            fixday = True
        if not byhour or hour in byhour:
            break
```
Here's an example:
If the initial value of `hour` is an odd number, say `23`, and the `byhour` tuple is, e.g., `(0, 6, 12, 18)`, then we have an endless loop if `interval` is even because `hour` will always be odd and, hence, `hour in byhour` is never `True`!

Because dateutil is used by matplotlib, this causes some plotting routines to freeze.

pull_request.title: Loop fix
pull_request.body:
Converted most of the `while True` loops to explicit `for` loops looping over a length after which the pattern repeats, then raise an error if the pattern hasn't broken by then. This should produce a desirable behavior that fixes #4 (though I think that there are certain endless-loop conditions which I'm currently only detecting in the iterator, not the constructor, because checking them in the constructor would involve a much more complicated logic because they involve interactions between the `byhour`, `byminute` and/or `bysecond` rules - either way I think they're likely exceedingly rare in practice).

I did a little refactoring in the looping logic, but not much since I think a lot of it won't end up being used in `rrule2` anyway. I'm a bit curious as to why we're explicitly handling the low-level operations of incrementing the day rather than incrementing a `datetime.datetime` object using `datetime.timedelta` objects - is this for the sake of performance or something? I can't imagine it would add much overhead, and it would be much easier to maintain.

I also converted the `by_` tuples to sets, because it doesn't seem that their order is ever used, but there are frequent calls to `in`, which will be considerably sped up by the use of sets. While I was doing that, I did some refactoring in the constructor which will make it easier to switch back if this change proves undesirable.

issue.title: Triangle should look nicer
issue.body:
This is related to #6 but it goes further. I have made a short video (only 8.5 MB) to explain well the problems there are with the triangle right now:

https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/2754299/TriangleAndZoom.mov

Basically, 
1) The triangle is not centred (at least on my configuration, macbook pro, Chrome).
2) The triangle is too short on the horizontal side. The vertical is perfect. So we are using the wrong ratio at least for this machine. Not sure how this changes on other machines
3) the grey rectangle is perfect in its dimensions, but the triangle does not finish where the grey triangle finishes
4) when a person sees the triangle at different zoom levels (zooming in or out of a page, for example if he has a very big monitor, or a very small one, or he cannot see very well) the triangle size does not change in a smooth way.

Note also that there is no effective need to keep a grey background around the triangle, so taking that away might not solve the ratio of the triangle, but at least make it look less ugly.

issue.title: Signing URLs for improved security
issue.body:
Pippin asked me to go ahead and open an issue here for discussion on a new implementation for improving the security of URLs that I built out as an add-on at the moment. Considering the implications of something like this, it'd be ideal to roll it into the core plugin, but may require breaking some currently valid URLs.

The basic premise is that URLs can be signed using a unique string, in this case `wp_salt()`, and when requested, the token can be checked to ensure none of the variables in the query string have been tampered with. This allows for passing non-sensitive data through the URL in the clear and being certain that it hasn't been changed. It essentially allows for more secure and concise URLs.

### Code

My implementation is available here for anyone wanting to try it out and offer feedback on how it could be improved or integrated: https://github.com/bradyvercher/EDD-Signed-URLs

The first three functions simply hook into EDD to modify and check the URLs, while the last three functions provide the API for signing URLs.

The concept will work with any URL structure, so my method of condensing everything into a colon delimited `eddfile` query arg isn't required (and that arg could even be renamed with a simple filter if desired).

### Breakage

As far as potentially breaking changes, existing URLs that haven't expired would quit working with this solution. It might be possible to run things side by side for a short while, but the current method would need to be deprecated at some point.

This would also decrease the reliance on using the `download_key` to look up a payment, instead using actual payment IDs, which might make things a little easier to work with. In that case, the current API utilizing the `download_key` might need to be augmented, or a new solution could be run side by side. I'm not sure if anyone is using the existing functions directly or not.

### Improvements

In any case, we're opening this up to see if anyone has ideas on implementing a solution like this without breaking anything. Feedback about improvements, suggestions on the default URL structure (is it worth trying to simplify?), and increasing security is welcome.

Feel free to correct me if I got anything wrong, Pippin.

comment.body:
Hmm, that's a good point. Without the separate URL parameters, it's more difficult to determine the expiration dates.

What if we were to add an expiration date parameter that is checked only if the token is verified? The expiration date could be included as its own parameter and also part of the token creation, that way it can't be changed.

issue.title: [WIP] major refactoring of architecture
issue.body:
|Q            |A  |
|---          |---|
|Bug Fix?     |yes|
|New Feature? |yes |
|BC Breaks?   |*yes!** |
|Deprecations?|no |
|Fixed Tickets| #26  |
|License      |MIT|

This a major refactoring of the search system architecture.

In summary the following has changed;

## ConditionOptimizers 

Formatters are renamed to ConditionOptimizers, and have an optional priority for sorting.

## Input processor changes

View to normalized value transformation now happens in the Input processor.
The SearchConditionBuilder does not use this technique.

Range bounds are now validated when processing, and not as an *optional* process afterwards.

To make InputProcessors reusable, configuration must be provided as first parameter of `process()`.

And last, all processors when testing now share the same assertions to ensure a correct result.

## Values 

To make locking the SearchCondition state easier and enforce a stricter OOP architecture value objects are now immutable and marked final.

`PatternMatch::getViewValue()` is removed as this method doesn't make sense for a string-only value object.

ValueGroups no longer keep track of errors, but ask the ValuesBag's and nested groups instead.

## Symfony validator

The Symfony validator extension is **finally** moved to its own repository and package.
As constraint validation is no longer needed for validating range-bounds.

## TODO

- [ ] Add support for locking the ValuesGroup and FieldSet.
- [ ] Check documentation for inconsistent usage of terms.
- [ ] Make tests for exporters uniform (same like input).
- [ ] Look for missing tests and documentation.
- [ ] Allow removing errors from a ValuesBag.

issue.title: [Vote] Which authentification mechanisms should we provide?
issue.body:
We currently provide:

- "formed based" authentication with Spring Security, which we have extended so you can invalidate sessions, have a better cookie theft feature, etc...
- OAuth2 authentification, which requires us to have our own server side implementation in MongoDB (and soon in Cassandra)

Both options are good and are two different approaches.

Now we have 4 other options that are currently opened tickets:

- #684 Support Spring Social
- #813 Use Json Web Tokens
- #892 x-auth-token authentication method
- #903 use Angular Token

Obviously, we can't support all of them, so we need to choose. From my personal point of view, what we already have is good enough, and I don't know if those other mechanisms are good/secured/useful.

So I'm opening this ticket to start a discussion and a vote, and close the mechanisms that we will not support.

comment.body:
..or at least don't close the poll yet. What is already in jhipster is fine for now. I wouldn't change much yet after only hearing from a few people on a poll that wasn't tweeted about. 
Jwt, oauth2 + openid connect is a powerful authentication/authorization combination with ietf standards and support from big players (jwt is authorization not authentication in itself but openid connect is authentication). I admit it isn't simple but I think it's worth it at the right time. 
If you do need to change direction right now, I wouldn't go far from what you currently have. 

I'm very interested in this topic and only saw this poll now!

pull_request.title: [WIP] Adding tests for estimators implementing `partial_fit` and a few other related fixes / enhancements
pull_request.body:
Attempting to fix #3896

**New `partial_fit` tests:**
The below tests are based off @arjoly's [suggestion](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/3896#issuecomment-64862823).

- [ ] 1. General tests
  * Assert that `partial_fit` returns `self` - Thanks @jnothman for [the suggestion.]
(https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/3896#issue-50330161)
  * Clone test... `assert clone(est).partial_fit == est.partial_fit`
- [x] 2. Check that an error is raised if the number of features changes from one partial fit to another.
- [x] 3. Estimator reset test
  * Check that doing `fit` after a set of `fit` / `partial_fit` restarts the estimator
  * Assert that `partial_fit` and then `fit` with a different number of features works without raising any Exceptions... - Thanks @amueller for [the suggestion](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/3907#issuecomment-68411916)
- [ ] 4. Multiple partial fit call tests
* Based on @jnothman [suggestion](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/3907#issuecomment-68478630)
- [x] 5. Check that classifier handles correctly the classes argument in the `partial_fit`.
  * a. Check if mismatch between `classes` argument and `np.unique(y_i)` for a particular pfit call raises `ValueError`.
  * b. Check that error is raised if `classes` is not specified during first `partial_fit` call.
- [ ] Fix modules which do not pass the above tests.
  * Fix `MiniBatchKMeans` to make it pass the 3rd test


**NOTE**

* `HashingVectorizer`'s `partial_fit` does nothing hence is skipped from tests...
* `MiniBatchDictionaryLearning` and `LSHForest` do not generallize well like other pfit capable estimators and hence `partial_fit` testing for the same should be done under its own dedicated tests.

issue.title: Trick for automatically serializing eagerly loaded associations?
issue.body: Just a minor issue that I'm struggling with at the moment. It appears that the default instance implementation of toJSON detects and automatically serializes any eagerly loaded associations on the model. However, the name that the associations are loaded under is the capitalized and pluralized name of the association. So if I have a 'Topic' model with a 'Category' association such that `Topic.belongsTo(Category)`, if I eagerly load the category with the topic, I get `topic.Category`. Obviously this is a trivial example but I'm wondering if there is some way to access a list of eagerly loaded associations from within the toJSON() instance method so that I can programmatically rename and serialize all of the eagerly loaded associations?

Hi, sorry that you're having difficulties!  The problem is that the Hoplon tutorials assume you're using boot 1, at [tailrecursion/boot](https://github.com/tailrecursion/boot).

Unfortunately we haven't ported Hoplon too boot 2 - the one at boot-clj/boot - yet, so if you want to both use hoplon and boot 2, you need to have booth boots installed.

Personally I have boot 1 installed as 'boot1' on my system, that way I can do `boot1 development` etc.

Use mktemp for temporary download directory

Using the current directory may not always be appropriate, for example in
the case where it will unnecessarily trigger a backup to be made.

The only risk with this change is that systems might not have a mktemp.
I am not aware of such a system, but have not tested on Windows. It is
working on a basic Ubuntu and OS X installation.

Fall back to hard coded download directory

If mktemp fails, fall back to a hard coded directory, per @nodakai's feedback.

Don't preserve line breaks in inline code

Closes #19323.

Add comments with type annotations.

This will hopefully help people with their first steps in Rust.

Fixes #16143.

Use rust-installer for installation

This is just a refactoring of the current installer so that Rust and Cargo
use the same codebase.

cc #16456

serialize: Avoid stray nul characters when auto-serializing char.

Fixes #19719.
Add coercions from *mut to *const and from &mut to *const.

rustc: Don't panic on corrupt metadata

Fix a panic where the compiler was looking at stale or old metadata.

See #19798, #19772, #19757, #19744, #19718, #19691.

Windows dbghelp strips leading underscores from symbols, so let's accept "ZN...E" form too.
Also, print PC displacement from symbols.

Deprecate more in-tree libs for crates.io

This commit deprecates a few more in-tree libs for their crates.io counterparts.
Note that this commit does not make use of the #[deprecated] tag to prevent
warnings from being generated for in-tree usage. Once #[unstable] warnings are
turned on then all external users will be warned to move.

These crates have all been duplicated in rust-lang/$crate repositories so
development can happen independently of the in-tree copies. We can explore at a
later date replacing the in-tree copies with the external copies, but at this
time the libraries have changed very little over the past few months so it's
unlikely for changes to be sent to both repos.

cc #19260

Change `VecMap`'s iterators to use wrapper structs instead of typedefs.

Using a type alias for iterator implementations is fragile since this
exposes the implementation to users of the iterator, and any changes
could break existing code.

This commit changes the iterators of `VecMap` to use
proper new types, rather than type aliases.  However, since it is
fair-game to treat a type-alias as the aliased type, this is a:

[breaking-change].

rustc: Start the deprecation of libserialize

The primary focus of Rust's stability story at 1.0 is the standard library.
All other libraries distributed with the Rust compiler are planned to
be #[unstable] and therfore only accessible on the nightly channel of Rust. One
of the more widely used libraries today is libserialize, Rust's current solution
for encoding and decoding types.

The current libserialize library, however, has a number of drawbacks:

* The API is not ready to be stabilize as-is and we will likely not have enough
  resources to stabilize the API for 1.0.
* The library is not necessarily the speediest implementations with alternatives
  being developed out-of-tree (e.g. serde from erickt).
* It is not clear how the API of Encodable/Decodable can evolve over time while
  maintaining backwards compatibility.

One of the major pros to the current libserialize, however, is
`deriving(Encodable, Decodable)` as short-hands for enabling serializing and
deserializing a type. This is unambiguously useful functionality, so we cannot
simply deprecate the in-tree libserialize in favor of an external crates.io
implementation.

For these reasons, this commit starts off a stability story for libserialize by
following these steps:

1. The deriving(Encodable, Decodable) modes will be deprecated in favor of a
   renamed deriving(RustcEncodable, RustcDecodable).
2. The in-tree libserialize will be deprecated in favor of an external
   rustc-serialize crate shipped on crates.io. The contents of the crate will be
   the same for now (but they can evolve separately).
3. At 1.0 serialization will be performed through
   deriving(RustcEncodable, RustcDecodable) and the rustc-serialize crate. The
   expansions for each deriving mode will change from `::serialize::foo` to
   `::rustc_serialize::foo`.

This story will require that the compiler freezes its implementation of
`RustcEncodable` deriving for all of time, but this should be a fairly minimal
maintenance burden. Otherwise the crate in crates.io must always maintain the
exact definition of its traits, but the implementation of json, for example, can
continue to evolve in the semver-sense.

The major goal for this stabilization effort is to pave the road for a new
official serialization crate which can replace the current one, solving many of
its downsides in the process. We are not assuming that this will exist for 1.0,
hence the above measures. Some possibilities for replacing libserialize include:

* If plugins have a stable API, then any crate can provide a custom `deriving`
  mode (will require some compiler work). This means that any new serialization
  crate can provide its own `deriving` with its own backing
  implementation, entirely obsoleting the current libserialize and fully
  replacing it.

* Erick is exploring the possibility of code generation via preprocessing Rust
  source files in the near term until plugins are stable. This strategy would
  provide the same ergonomic benefit that `deriving` does today in theory.

So, in summary, the current libserialize crate is being deprecated in favor of
the crates.io-based rustc-serialize crate where the `deriving` modes are
appropriately renamed. This opens up space for a later implementation of
serialization in a more official capacity while allowing alternative
implementations to be explored in the meantime.

Concretely speaking, this change adds support for the `RustcEncodable` and
`RustcDecodable` deriving modes. After a snapshot is made warnings will be
turned on for usage of `Encodable` and `Decodable` as well as deprecating the
in-tree libserialize crate to encurage users to use rustc-serialize instead.

Fix mispelling in char.rs error message

Error message has wrong spelling ("radix is to high").
libsyntax: Make deriving also respect where bounds.
libsyntax: Output where clauses in pretty printer for structs.

Modify `regex::Captures::{at,name}` to return `Option`

Closes #14602.  As discussed in that issue, the existing `at` and `name`
functions represent two different results with the empty string:

1. Matched the empty string.
2. Did not match anything.

Consider the following example.  This regex has two named matched
groups, `key` and `value`. `value` is optional:

```rust
// Matches "foo", "foo;v=bar" and "foo;v=".
regex!(r"(?P<key>[a-z]+)(;v=(?P<value>[a-z]*))?");
```

We can access `value` using `caps.name("value")`, but there's no way for
us to distinguish between the `"foo"` and `"foo;v="` cases.

Early this year, @BurntSushi recommended modifying the existing `at` and
`name` functions to return `Option`, instead of adding new functions to
the API.

This is a [breaking-change], but the fix is easy:

- `refs.at(1)` becomes `refs.at(1).unwrap_or("")`.
- `refs.name(name)` becomes `refs.name(name).unwrap_or("")`.

InvariantLifetime is Copy-able

Both ContravariantLifetime and CovariantLifetime are marked as Copy,
so it makes sense for InvariantLifetime to be as well.
Fix indentation in a code example in the ownership guide.

commits.message:
staging: binder: Change binder mutex to rtmutex.

Surfaceflinger uses binder heavily to receive/send frames from applications
while compositing the screen. Change the binder mutex to an rt mutex to minimize
instances where high priority surfaceflinger binder work is blocked by lower
priority binder ipc.

Signed-off-by: Riley Andrews <riandrews@google.com>
Change-Id: I086a715267648448f0c5f62b037a3093d1079a79

Revert "fastcharge: initial adaptation for Nexus 4"

This reverts commit 797826780e7a8bcbc9d933a65254fa5c01fe97c2.

USB force fast charging

-Use base from Chad Froebel <chadfroebel@gmail.com> so we continue to
use the same generic sysfs mechanism

-Referenced franco's git for drivers/usb/otg/msm_otg.c changes
https://github.com/franciscofranco/mako/commit/5a8a4c8e23c7e1df39c740b9ce1d5dda20b0ede3

Off by default

Turn on:
echo 1 > /sys/kernel/fast_charge/force_fast_charge

Turn off:
echo 0 > /sys/kernel/fast_charge/force_fast_charge

msm_thermal: Introduce Dynamic thermal control ;)

When user changed cpu max clock, the max clock is retored by msm_thermal settings.

This patch fix this issue and control thermal dynamically.

When user changed the cpu max clock, msm_thermal settings will be automatically change.
The clock settings in msm_thermal, will be set based on changed cpu max clock.
And thermal settings in msm_thermal, will be optimize based on current cpu clock settings.

This function enabled by default.
You can turn off this function by typing,
echo 0 > /sys/kernel/msm_thermal/conf/dynamic_thermal_control
Or re-enable by typing,
echo 1 > /sys/kernel/msm_thermal/conf/dynamic_thermal_control

If dynamic_thermal_control set to 1, you can't adjust msm_thermal settings. It will be restored automatically by this function.
If you want to adjust msm_thermal settings manuaaly, turn off this function. And use your device with caution.

If you do not want whole of thermal control functions, just turn off thermal throttling in the kernel control app. (Not recommended!)

issue.title: Chrome on Windows disables non-web store HTTPS Everywhere on restart
issue.body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. In Chrome on Windows, install HTTPS Everywhere directly from EFF (download the .crx, drag and drop into Extensions page).
2. Restart Chrome.

Expected result:

HTTPS Everywhere stays installed.

Actual result:

On next startup, a notice appears in the upper right saying "Unsupported extensions disabled. To make Chrome safer, we disabled some extensions that aren't listed in the Chrome Web Store and may have been added without your knowledge.

 - HTTPS Everywhere"

On the Extensions page, HTTPS Everywhere is greyed out, disabled, and the checkbox to re-enable it is greyed out. Enabling developer mode doesn't fix it, nor does dragging in the .crx again. Deleting the extension and dragging back in the .crx works until the next restart.

We should ask Google about this.

comment.body:
There are two options to workaround this.

One is extracting the CRX to a new folder in the computer and use programing mode to load the extension from the folder.

Another one is, the one I use for archival purposes, download the CRX from Chrome webstore using "Give me CRX": https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/give-me-crx/acpimoebmfjpfnbhjgdgiacjfebmmmci

Apparently there is some method of certificate authentication in CRX files and those downloaded from eff's website mismatch the copies at google's servers.

Regards,
NewEraCracker

issue.body:
Running ssadump on [this go program](http://play.golang.org/p/JHUgaI-2sq) produces a panic: 

    panic: interface conversion: interface is reflect.rtype, not *reflect.rtype

With go gc 1.4 on GNU/Linux there is none. 

The full invocation, output produced, and golang version is given in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/rocky/6f4f1955cdf8addaeb92). 

Looking at the Go code:

    u8 reflect.Type = reflect.TypeOf(uint8(0))
    byteSlice reflect.Type = reflect.SliceOf(u8)

I am just as confused as ssadump. Here is *reflect.SliceOf* in *reflect/type.go*:

    func SliceOf(t Type) Type {
    typ := t.(*rtype)
    ...

The ssadump error message makes sense to me in that the passed-in type is a `reflect.rtype`, not and `*reflect.rtype` which is what  appears to be the use in *reflect.SliceOf*. 

So what is it in Go that makes it okay to have these things not give a type error?

issue.title: ENH: sparse: speedup LIL matrix slicing
issue.body:
The current implementation for slicing LIL matrices is very pessimal. Replace it with a more optimal implementation.

Gives a factor of ~1/density speedup:
```
In []: A = rand(3000, 3000, density=1e-3, format="lil")

# Before (9ccc68475)
In [4]: %timeit A[::2,::-2]
10 loops, best of 3: 87.5 ms per loop

# After (d47e27b0)
In [4]: %timeit A[::2,::-2]
1000 loops, best of 3: 603 µs per loop
```
Gives speedups also for smaller slices:
```
# Before
In [5]: %timeit A[3,:]
1000 loops, best of 3: 213 µs per loop
In [6]: %timeit A[:,3]
1000 loops, best of 3: 901 µs per loop
In [7]: %timeit A[1:5,1:5]
10000 loops, best of 3: 83.3 µs per loop

# After
In [5]: %timeit A[3,:]
10000 loops, best of 3: 38.8 µs per loop
In [6]: %timeit A[:,3]
1000 loops, best of 3: 702 µs per loop
In [7]: %timeit A[1:5,1:5]
10000 loops, best of 3: 40.3 µs per loop
```
(Column slices in LIL are still problematic, but that's due to the matrix format.)

**EDIT** updated benchmarks

issue.title: Choose a license
issue.body:
Right now, ServeSimple doesn't have a license. That's not because there aren't enough to choose from.

With ServeSimple, I mostly care about keeping it free. I don't know much about the legalities, but I do know enough to realize that "free" means different things to different people. Free to modify and keep closed if someone wishes (MIT-ish) or free and always remaining open (GPL-ish). Seems more like philosophy than law. (Although [maybe everything leads there eventually](http://flowingdata.com/2011/06/08/all-roads-lead-to-philosophy-on-wikipedia/)?)

Since I intend to offer free hosting of ServeSimple, I think the biggest thing I want to prevent is someone else charging a non-profit for hosting an instance ServeSimple as ServeSimple. (But, maybe that's not such a big deal? Argh!)

As this is a free project, we'll want to leverage as much third-party and quality software that already exists. Does choosing one path or another restrict our use of key components?

Some options:

* MIT/Apache
* GPL

comment.body:
@joshua1 what do you mean? Classes are a basic programming construct you can use anywhere. This library just simplifies working with classical inheritance in Javascript similar to how Coffeescript does.

Where you put your code depends on how you want to structure the overall application, that's pretty much a matter of taste or conventions. E.g: I never use a `lib` folder and also don't think it's a great naming convention because it's way to general and just shows that you have no clear idea about this code.

issue.body: What versions are being used? Seems like 1.0.1 isn't: https://github.com/flaub/openssl-net/issues/4 and hence we aren't supporting TLS1.1, TLS1.2 or authenticated TLS like GCM or perfect forward secrecy.

issue.title: de-select (reset) multiselection fields
issue.body:
Talking about $eventData['properties']['ep_disable_markup_* 

I just discovered being unable to reset an already selected disabled markup plugin via the entryforms entryproperties markup hook. (It is not a javascript issue!)

1. Edit entry with CKEDITOR and disable nl2br via multiselect
2. Save your entry
3. Via sidebar get entries request call this entry again and de-select the multiselect selection ([CTRL]+marked option)
3. Save your entry
4. Via sidebar get entries request, call this entry again and see the multiselect has not changed.

I already have a full working proposel adding a NONE constant reset option field for this, if it has selected options, but maybe this will happen to us on more places too....?!

Anybody for this?
